title: Knowledge & Logic
overview: Logic is how AI knows things — through rules and True/False statements, not common sense

blocks.title: What is Propositional Logic?
blocks.body: Logic is how AI knows things — through rules and True/False statements, not common sense
bullets: Propositional logic uses statements that are either True or False
AND — both sides must be True for result to be True
OR — at least one side must be True
NOT — reverses the value (NOT True = False)
This concept is fundamental to AI development.

analogy.title: Think of Logic as a Detective
analogy.description: Use facts and rules to deduce conclusions

code.output:
Both true → deduce conclusion
True → deduce fact

blocks.title: Evaluating Logic Expressions
blocks.instructions: Run the code to see how AND, OR, and NOT evaluate different logical expressions.
blocks.starterCode:
# Evaluate these logic expressions
print("True and True:", True and True)
print("True and False:", True and False)
print("True or False:", True or False)
print("not True:", not True)
print("(True or False) and not False:", (True or False) and not False)
blocks.solution:
print("True and True:", True and True)
print("True and False:", True and False)
print("True or False:", True or False)
print("not True:", not True)
print("(True or False) and not False:", (True or False) and not False)
blocks.hint: AND needs both True, OR needs at least one True, NOT flips the value.
blocks.expectedOutput:
True and True: True
True and False: False
True or False: True
not True: False
(True or False) and not False: True

blocks.title: What is Knowledge Base & Inference?
blocks.body: AI stores facts and rules in a Knowledge Base and uses Inference to derive new facts
bullets: A Knowledge Base is a collection of facts and rules AI uses to reason
Inference means deriving new facts from existing ones
IF-THEN rules: If it is raining AND I am outside, THEN I get wet
Real-world uses: medical diagnosis systems, FAQ chatbots, Google Knowledge Panel
This concept is fundamental to AI development.

analogy.title: Think of Inference as a Puzzle Solver
analogy.description: Apply rules to known facts to derive new facts

blocks.title: Building a Knowledge Base
blocks.instructions: Build a knowledge base with facts and use inference rules to derive new facts.
blocks.starterCode:
# Build a knowledge base with inference
facts = {"has_wings": True, "is_bird": True}
# Rule: if has_wings AND is_bird THEN can_fly
if facts["has_wings"] and facts["is_bird"]:
    facts["can_fly"] = True
    print("Inferred: can_fly")
print(f"Facts: {facts}")
blocks.hint: A Knowledge Base stores facts. Inference applies logical rules to derive new facts.
blocks.expectedOutput:
Inferred: can_fly
Facts: {'has_wings': True, 'is_bird': True, 'can_fly': True}

blocks.title: What is How AI Uses Logic?
blocks.body: Follow these steps to build a logical reasoning system.
bullets: Step 1: Define your facts — what is True and what is False in your world
Step 2: Write IF-THEN rules — connect facts to conclusions
Step 3: Build a Knowledge Base — store all facts and rules together
Step 4: Run Inference — AI combines facts and rules to reach new conclusions
This concept is fundamental to AI development.

analogy.title: Think of Knowledge as a Family Tree

code.code:
family = [("Alice", "parent", "Bob"), ("Bob", "parent", "Charlie")]
for a, r, b in family:
    print(f"{a} → {b}")
print("Inferred: Alice is grandparent of Charlie")
code.output:
Alice → Bob
Bob → Charlie
Inferred: Alice is grandparent of Charlie

blocks.title: Propositional Logic Evaluator
blocks.code:
# Simple logic inference engine
def AND(a, b): return a and b
def OR(a, b): return a or b
def NOT(a): return not a
def IMPLIES(a, b): return not a or b

# Knowledge base: If it rains, the ground gets wet
rains = True
wet = IMPLIES(rains, True)
print(f"Rains -> Wet: {wet}")

# Is the ground wet?
print(f"Ground is wet: {AND(rains, wet)}")
blocks.expectedOutput:
Rains -> Wet: True
Ground is wet: True

keyTakeaways.text: Logic uses True/False statements called propositions
AND needs both sides True; OR needs at least one True; NOT reverses
IF-THEN rules connect facts to conclusions
A Knowledge Base stores all facts and rules AI uses
Inference derives new facts from existing ones — like solving a puzzle
Real uses: medical diagnosis, chatbots, Google Knowledge Panel
